title: Vectorial Boolean nonlinearity beyond the Nyberg threshold
summary: Prove a uniform upper bound on component nonlinearity for maps beyond the Nyberg threshold; tightness remains open in this record.

formal_statement.body: For every $k\ge3$, $k<m<2k$, and $F:\mathbb F_2^{2k}\to\mathbb F_2^m$, prove $\operatorname{NL}(F)\le 2^{2k-1}-2^{k-1}-2$, where $\operatorname{NL}(F)$ is the minimum scalar nonlinearity over nonzero components (equivalently the joint Walsh definition). This record does not claim that the bound is tight for every $(k,m)$.

scope.domain: Vectorial Boolean functions and component nonlinearity
scope.unresolved_remainder: Tightness of the general upper bound for all admissible (n,m) remains outside the public record.

progress.summary: Nyberg's threshold rules out vectorial bentness once the output dimension exceeds the half-dimension threshold.
Coding-theoretic work formulates the optimization problem and records non-tight general bounds.

progress.summary: Lean proves the displayed uniform upper bound for every k >= 3 and k < m < 2k, including Walsh inversion and Parseval, an internal proof of the Nyberg bound, the even-component hyperplane, simultaneous congruence normalization, and the odd-fibre contradiction; tightness is outside scope.
